calls.reason: The only independent source, Wu et al. (NAACL 2024), cuts both ways: models leaned heavily on familiar patterns but still did nontrivially well on altered tasks. 'Reasoning' is undefined, and the riddle output is documented only in Marcus's post.
ARC Prize and the AGI Society both decline to call Astra AGI, and no study shows symbolic methods are necessary. With no deadline and no agreed AGI test, this necessity claim cannot be called yet.

The July 2024 regulators' joint statement points to incumbents' accumulated advantages but treats them as a risk. Meta's claim that Llama was competitive covers only model capability. Neither settles whether any company had a moat.

More than two years later, the Reuters Institute survey found weekly generative AI use nearly doubled by mid-2025. OpenAI's own 2026 data, a weaker source, also shows ChatGPT adoption growing. Even on a loose reading of 'soon', there was no flame-out.
This is an open-ended forecast framed as an intuition. OpenAI says hallucinations persisted as of Sept 2025, which fits the claim, but no finite date can confirm 'never'.

Meta's Llama 3.1 materials support the picture of scaling, similar GPT-4-level results and ongoing hallucinations. But Anthropic's capability gains and Meta's other research complicate it, and there is no data on how investment was split.
